business_scope.primary_industry_name: Retail Sale via Internet - DTC Brand Webstore

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: South Korea (Yuhan Hoesa private limited company under the Korean Commercial Act)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Free Trade Agreement between the Government of the Republic of Korea and the Government of the United States of America (KORUS FTA)
Convention between the Republic of Korea and the United States of America for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income
Free Trade Agreement between the Government of the Republic of Korea and the Government of the People's Republic of China
Agreement between the Government of the Republic of Korea and the Government of Canada for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Information (Specific Financial Information Act), Act No. 17784, as amended, Articles 5 bis and 5 ter; Financial Transaction Reports Act, Act No. 17355, as amended; Real Name Financial Transactions and Guarantee Act, Article 3; Enforcement Decree of the Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Information prescribing the 25% beneficial-ownership threshold; Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) Beneficial Owner Identification and Customer Due Diligence Regulations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the foreign corporate parent or corporate shareholder/UBO entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or competent registrar of the jurisdiction of incorporation of the foreign parent/UBO entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the issuing jurisdiction is a party to the Hague Apostille Convention: notarization (if required by the issuer), then an Apostille certificate issued by the designated competent authority, submitted directly to the Korean registry and bank; do not add Korean consular legalization. If the issuing jurisdiction is not an Apostille Convention state: certify at the local Ministry of Foreign Affairs or equivalent and then legalize at the Korean Embassy or Consulate having consular jurisdiction over the issuing state; apostille is not used. The two routes are mutually exclusive and are never combined sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Active Corporate Status of the foreign corporate shareholder/UBO entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Same competent corporate registrar as the foreign parent/UBO entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague path: apostille only from the issuing state's competent authority and direct submission. Non-Hague path: Korean consular legalization after local authentication of the certificate. Do not apply an apostille in a non-Hague state, and do not apply consular legalization in a Hague state; the respective paths are parallel, separate, and mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney of the foreign corporate shareholder authorizing the formation of the Korean Yuhan Hoesa and appointing the domestic incorporator/representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors or equivalent governing body of the foreign corporate shareholder/UBO entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The resolution must be notarized by a notary public in the shareholder's home country; if that country is an Apostille Convention state, attach an apostille from the competent authority; if not, attach Korean consular legalization after the requisite local authentication. The apostille and consular legalization routes are alternative and exclusive; do not chain them.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Articles of Association of the Korean Yuhan Hoesa (Yuhan Hoesa Jeong-gwan), including the name, purpose, capital, and consent to the corporate governance regime
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean notary public executing the statutory articles for Yuhan Hoesa formation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The Korean articles are notarized before a Korean notary and lodged with the Korean registry; no apostille is needed for domestic registration. If a certified copy must be used abroad, the receiving state's authentication rule applies: Korean apostille if the receiving state is an Apostille Convention member, or Korean consular legalization if the receiving state is not a member. This export path is separate from and never merged with the foreign-shareholder document paths.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the foreign corporate shareholder/UBO, including relationship age, account conduct, and sanction/AML standing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Shareholder's principal bank in the shareholder's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank reference letter must be signed by the bank's compliance officer and notarized; the notarized letter is then either apostilled by the issuing state's competent authority (Hague path) or, in a non-Hague state, authenticated locally and then legalized by the Korean Embassy/Consulate. The bank reference letter must be no older than 30 days at delivery, with a 90-day overall validity window; apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive alternatives.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Every director, shareholder, UBO, signatory, agent, and beneficial owner of the Korean Yuhan Hoesa must be screened against the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit domestic warnings and blacklists, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons list, the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, EU and UK OFSI sanctions lists, the World Bank debarment list, and global adverse-media/PEP databases before filing. Any candidate identified as a PEP, close associate, or family member of a PEP is subject to enhanced due diligence, including documented source of wealth and source of funds, written approval by the AML compliance officer, and ongoing transaction monitoring. Verified identifiers must be retained for at least five years after closure and refreshed on any material change.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registry Office (IROS) through www.iros.go.kr, supplemented by the Court Administration Office of the Supreme Court and the Korean Commercial Registration name-search service
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Korean Commercial Act, the trade name of a Yuhan Hoesa must be expressed in the Korean Hangul alphabet. The registered name is composed in four tiers: (1) a distinctive brand/creative element; (2) the business object or purpose description; (3) the statutory suffix 'Yuhan Hoesa' (private limited company); and (4) if required for distinguishability, a local-registry identifier, d/b/a, or auxiliary trade name. A foreign brand name may be used only as an auxiliary trade name in the business registration certificate and must be either transliterated into Hangul phonetically or displayed with the Hangul primary name; Roman or Chinese characters alone cannot be the statutory corporate name. The proposed name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered corporate name or protected mark in the Korean database.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the IROS returns a name rejection, the applicant must, within seven days, request the registry officer's written statement of reasons, then submit a reconsideration request to the same Supreme Court Internet Registry Office with the original application log, the name-search result, and a written explanation of how the proposed name is distinctive and outside the prohibited/sensitive category. If the registry officer confirms rejection, the applicant may file an immediate appeal with the competent district court under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act within 14 days of the written refusal, attaching all prior rejection documents and a revised name or legal argument. The filing must enclose the court-fee receipt and the applicant's proof of authority, and may be accompanied by an amended name variant.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office, commercial mailbox, or P.O. box is not acceptable as the statutory registered office of a Korean Yuhan Hoesa engaged in ISIC 4791 DTC internet retail. The National Tax Service and municipal tax authority require a physical place of business for electronic tax invoice issuance, inventory control, and dispatch operations; Korean banks and payment partners, including those supporting Shopify Payments, PayPal, and Stripe settlement, will reject a mail-forwarding virtual address as evidence of commercial substance and may refuse to open a corporate operating account or approve merchant settlement. A serviced office with a dedicated workstation, physical signage, an executed lease in the company's name, and actual access to the premises may satisfy the place-of-business standard if it is not a mere mail-scanning suite and the e-tax invoice address matches the registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: approximately 25% within the first 18 months for a new foreign-owned DTC e-commerce company. Checklist: (1) physically staff the registered office during business hours; (2) maintain the signed lease, utility bills, and photographs of the premises; (3) keep e-commerce inventory, fulfillment, and dispatch records on site; (4) display the registered trade name and tax invoice number at the entrance; (5) ensure the domestic representative can attend within two hours of a request; (6) keep the business registration certificate conspicuously posted; (7) match the registered-office address to the bank account address and the Shopify store terms address. An unannounced visit from the municipal tax office or registry office is triggered by VAT filing anomalies, cross-border payment reversals, or inconsistent invoice addresses.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Supreme Court of Korea, Court Administration Office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory online certificate/inquiry fee tariff of approximately KRW 6,000 for an issued search record

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certificate of Corporate Registration extract of the foreign parent/UBO entity and Korean registered address proof
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registry office of the relevant jurisdiction
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory corporate register extract fee of approximately KRW 5,000 per certified extract

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of the Korean Yuhan Hoesa Articles of Association
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Korean Notary Public appointed by the Korean Ministry of Justice
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial fee schedule fixed by the Ministry of Justice, approximately KRW 100,000

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate registration license tax and education surtax for incorporation of a Yuhan Hoesa
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Local tax authority / district court registry office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Local Tax Act tariff; KRW 80,000 registration license tax plus 20% education tax

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Authorized judicial scrivener (beopmusa) professional fee for preparing and filing the Korean incorporation registration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Authorized judicial scrivener engaged by the company
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark in Seoul of KRW 750,000 to KRW 1,200,000 for a low-capital Yuhan Hoesa with foreign shareholders

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille of the foreign corporate parent/UBO documentary set (Certificate of Incorporation, Good Standing, Board Resolution/Power of Attorney, and Bank Reference Letter) under the Hague Apostille path
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign competent authority of the issuing state (e.g., Secretary of State or Foreign Ministry)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Foreign apostille fee schedule, typically USD 25 to USD 150 per document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Korean consular legalization of the foreign corporate parent/UBO documentary set in a non-Hague Apostille state
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Embassy of the Republic of Korea in the country of issuance
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Korean consular fee schedule, typically USD 150 to USD 300 per document for authentication/legalization

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial serviced-office place of business for three months, with dedicated desk, signage, and lease documentation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Seoul serviced-office provider under a commercial lease
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Seoul market benchmark of USD 500 to USD 800 per month for a dedicated desk and meeting-room access

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Part IV Chapter V on Yuhan Hoesa, Articles 287 et seq.; Foreign Investment Promotion Act Articles 4 and 5; Commercial Registration Rules of the Supreme Court.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Division of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the company registered office; online counterpart is the Supreme Court Registration Information Network (i-RO).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Limited Liability Company, filed in the prescribed form together with certified Articles of Incorporation and supporting corporate records.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None under the Commercial Act for a Yuhan Hoesa. The Articles of Incorporation determine the total amount of contributions and each member contribution. There is no statutory minimum paid-up capital and no compulsory blocked escrow account in the registry. For foreign investors in Korea, a foreign investment report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act is required before contribution if the amount is at least KRW 100,000,000 or the investor seeks management participation. The contribution must be paid in foreign currency through a registered foreign exchange bank, and evidence of remittance must be preserved for corporate registration and tax purposes.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF MANAGERS RESOLUTION OF YUHANGHOESA (LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY), SOUTH KOREA. ADOPTED ON [DATE] BY THE INITIAL MEMBERS AND MANAGERS OF THE COMPANY. RECITALS: (A) The company has been formed as a Yuhan Hoesa under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea and is recorded under the corporate identity stated in the task payload. (B) The founding members have executed the Articles of Incorporation setting out the total amount of contributions, the amount contributed by each member, the object of the company, the location of the registered office, the method of representation, the fiscal year, and the term of existence. (C) The initial managers have received the contribution schedules and are satisfied that the conditions precedent for registration have been satisfied or will be satisfied before the filing is delivered to the Registry Division. (D) The company intends to operate a DTC brand webstore through internet retail channels under ISIC 4791 and NAICS 454110. NOW THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS: 1. RESOLVED, that the Articles of Incorporation and the subscription statement attached as Exhibit A are ratified, accepted and confirmed in their entirety; that the contributions in cash or authorized non-cash property are approved for each member; and that no contribution shall be returned except upon a valid dissolution or statutory reduction permitted under the Commercial Act. 2. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the company is fixed at [full Korean street address] within the jurisdiction of [district court registration office], and the Republic of Korea is the jurisdiction in which the company is managed and controlled. 3. RESOLVED, that [name] be and hereby is appointed Representative Manager of the company and [name] be and hereby is appointed Finance Manager. Each of them shall have authority to act singly in ordinary-course administration, to execute bank mandates, to open and operate deposit and settlement accounts, and to appoint and remove local agents for corporate maintenance, but all instruments creating security, transferring real property, or approving annual financial statements shall require a resolution of the members or managers. 4. RESOLVED, that the Representative Manager is authorized to apply for the registration of incorporation with the competent District Court Registry, to register the corporate seal, to obtain business registration with the National Tax Service, to make foreign investment report filings, and to execute all such applications, powers of attorney, consents and certificates as may be required. 5. RESOLVED, that any two managers, or one manager accompanied by the corporate seal, are jointly authorized to sign banking mandates, payment processor agreements with Shopify Payments, PayPal, Stripe or any local gateway, and to receive funds and disburse lawful expenses; the Finance Manager is authorized to certify payment instructions to the bank. 6. RESOLVED, that the statutory books of the company, including the member register, contribution ledger, minutes, and adopted financial records, be established at the registered office and maintained in the Korean language or bilingual versions, and that the fiscal year shall end on 31 December of each calendar year. 7. RESOLVED, that the Representative Manager is authorized to obtain such domestic and cross-border authorizations as are legally advisable, including data protection instruments under the Personal Information Protection Act, tax invoice registrations, and postal or consumer protection registrations, and to engage the formation counsel and accountants. 8. RESOLVED, that this resolution is effective as of [date], may be executed in counterparts, and may be produced as prima facie evidence of authority in any bank, tax or judicial proceeding.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Determination of foreign investment report requirements and submission via the Korea Foreign Investment System
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) through the Korea Foreign Investment System (KFIS); authorized foreign exchange bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Review the ownership plan and determine whether the founding non-resident is required to file a foreign investment report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. A report is mandatory when the contribution amount is at least KRW 100,000,000 or the investor intends to obtain management control or voting rights linked to the Korean company. The report is submitted before cash remittance through KFIS, operated by KOTRA or an authorized foreign exchange bank. The applicant must prepare an original power of attorney, passport copy, draft articles, pro-forma financing plan and bank references. After approval, the system issues a foreign investment report certificate evidencing the lawful external payment route for the capital.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If KFIS rejects the report for incomplete documentation, resubmit within 14 days with corrected notarized documents. If the report is late, file a voluntary report with KOTRA and seek counsel to regularize any administrative penalty or foreign exchange violation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation, execution and notarization of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean notary public or licensed legal counsel in the Republic of Korea
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation in Korean containing the company trade name, corporate object, total amount of contributions, contribution of each member, registered office, number and authority of managers, method of representation, fiscal year end, and provisions for amendments, transfer of equity and dissolution. All founding members must execute the articles before the notary or with notarized signature authentication. An English translation should be prepared for foreign payment providers and banks. The corporate name should be checked for conflict through the Supreme Court company name search system. Foreign signatures should be notarized and apostilled if required by local authorities.
required_dossiers: English translation of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or counsel identifies a discrepancy in names, addresses or contribution amounts, prepare and execute amended articles or a typed correction within 5 days. If apostille is rejected due to signature mismatch, re-sign before a notary in the investor home jurisdiction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of incorporation with the District Court Registry Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Court Registration Division with territorial jurisdiction; Supreme Court Registration Information Network (i-RO) for electronic filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Limited Liability Company in the court-prescribed form. Attach the certified Articles of Incorporation, evidence of contribution payment or deposit if capital has been paid, a certificate of foreign investment report if applicable, member identity documentation, corporate seal certificate, power of attorney and proof of payment of the registration fee. Review the draft registry record for the company trade name, object, registered office, managers, representative manager, and announcement method. Submit to the court registry and request immediate issuance of a Certificate of Company Registration and certified corporate register transcript.
required_dossiers: Application for company registration in court-prescribed form
Certificate of foreign investment report if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a correction order or supplement request, complete the stated correction within the statutory response period, normally 14 days, and resubmit the certified corrected instrument. If the court refuses registration, apply for a new filing with the missing certificate or appeal through the applicable objection procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business registration with the National Tax Service for corporate income tax and value added tax purposes
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service, local district tax office having jurisdiction over the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the court registration certificate, file the Business Registration Application at the local tax office. Attach the certificate of company registration, Articles of Incorporation, registered corporate seal certificate, lease agreement or floor plan proving an accessible physical location, and identification documents for managers and foreign beneficial owners. Choose the filing basis for value added tax and corporate tax. The tax office will issue the business registration certificate with the business registration number. For e-commerce and DTC sales, ensure the tax office classification code matches online retail and provide a test account if the Shopify store or payment gateway requires tax invoice capability.
required_dossiers: Certificate of company registration issued by the court
Lease agreement or real floor plan
Passport or alien registration card copy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office queries the physical location, produce the lease contract and an on-site photograph. If the representative manager cannot attend, present a notarized power of attorney and re-issue the application. If the business is suspended due to insufficient address, convert to a temporary ordinary business place certificate and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate bank account opening, payment processor onboarding and e-commerce compliance clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial banks in Korea; local PSP or acquiring bank; Korea Financial Intelligence Unit compliance desk for AML reporting; Personal Information Protection authorities for data processing compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate bank account in the company name using the certificate of company registration, business registration certificate, corporate seal certificate, a board or managers resolution approving the account, and identification for all beneficial owners. The bank will perform customer due diligence and may require a detailed business description of the DTC brand store, expected monthly sales, payment rail structure and marketing channels. After the account is open, apply for merchant acceptance with a domestic acquiring bank or link Shopify Payments, PayPal, Stripe or a local gateway to the corporate account. Prepare Korean-language privacy notices and consent records under the Personal Information Protection Act, consumer refund and reshipment policies, tax invoice settings, and the company website terms of sale before transactional operations begin.
required_dossiers: Privacy policy and PIPA consent forms
Merchant application for Shopify Payments or PayPal or Stripe or local PSP
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional beneficial ownership documentation, provide a corporate tree showing all natural persons holding more than 25 percent. If the PSP rejects the application for lack of confirmable website information, provide the live URL, local address, privacy policy and refund policy, then apply to an alternate domestic acquiring bank.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - no industrial, manufacturing, chemical assembly or warehousing operation under ISIC 4791 and NAICS 454110.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - DTC brand webstore is an internet retail operation and does not require a physical manufacturing or wholesale operating license at formation.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - Ministry of Environment not triggered for pure e-commerce retail.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - no site-based industrial activity; no full EIA report, prior environmental review, or simple environmental registration is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no wastewater discharge, VOC emission, or hazardous waste generation thresholds apply to the company formation or webstore activities.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable at formation stage because the company does not occupy a manufacturing, chemical or warehousing site. If an office, showroom, or fulfillment warehouse is opened in South Korea later, the company must obtain a Certificate of Fire Prevention Facilities from the local district fire station, an ordinary business place occupancy or eviction certificate, and comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Act duties for employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; electronic filing via the HomeTax portal (hometax.go.kr). Export customs clearance is administered by the Korea Customs Service through the UNI-PASS electronic declaration system (unipass.customs.go.kr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: determine Korean tax nexus; a foreign non-resident DTC operator without a fixed place of business, personnel, warehouse, or permanent establishment in Korea will be treated as a non-resident business operator for VAT and Corporate Income Tax, and must appoint a Korean tax representative. Step 2: execute a power of attorney in favour of a tax representative (individual resident in Korea or a Korean corporation) and obtain the representative's consent. Step 3: file the Business Registration Application (사업자등록신청서) through HomeTax or through the authorised tax representative using the NTS non-resident registration channel, attaching the foreign entity's certificate of incorporation, constitutional documents, board resolution on registration, tax representative's power of attorney and identity evidence, and any underlying foreign tax registration. Step 4: NTS validates the application and issues a 10-digit Business Registration Number (BRN; 사업자등록번호), which simultaneously constitutes the VAT identification number and corporate taxpayer file for domestic tax administration. Step 5: complete the VAT registrant file, e-tax invoice enrolment, and list any Korean logistics providers; for a remote Shopify DTC operation, the BRN is issued without a Korean warehousing address unless the cross-border flow creates a physical import, distribution or fulfilment PE. Step 6: maintain continuous tax filing through HomeTax; any change in tax representative, Korean place of business, or address must be filed with the competent district tax office within 15 days.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. South Korea does not operate a check-the-box or elective pass-through classification regime. A Yuhan Hoesa with its head office or place of effective management in Korea is legally classified as a resident corporation and taxed at the corporate income tax rate schedule on worldwide income; hybrid mismatch recharacterisation rules are mandatory anti-abuse provisions and not taxpayer elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Korean Value-Added Tax Act (부가가치세법)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no general turnover exemption for a domestic Korean DTC entity: every entrepreneur must register for VAT with NTS within 20 days of business commencement, and the same 10-digit BRN serves as the VAT ID. Small businesses with annual VAT-exclusive taxable supplies not exceeding KRW 80 million may elect the simplified taxable person regime, but cannot avoid registration. For a foreign non-resident supplier without a local PE, VAT registration is mandatory when the prior calendar year's VAT-exclusive supply of electronic/digital services to unregistered Korean recipients exceeds KRW 30 million; the NTS commissioner may also require registration to protect the Korean tax base.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Korea mandates electronic tax invoices (e-tax invoices) for VAT-registered businesses issuing taxable sales invoices. The e-tax invoice must be transmitted to the NTS via the HomeTax e-tax invoice service, which accepts XML through the official HomeTax API/EDI/web upload channel. There is no pre-issuance fiscal authorisation stamp or real-time clearance gate: the NTS validates the transmission automatically, returns an acceptance result for the invoice to remain compliant, and cross-matches seller-issued and buyer-received invoices in near real time. Anti-fraud functions include automated reconciliation against customs declarations, foreign currency settlement records, and VAT returns; non-transmission, late transmission, or false e-tax invoices attract separate additional tax penalties and loss of input VAT deduction.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically exported from the Republic of Korea are zero-rated under Article 19 of the Value-Added Tax Act, regardless of the DTC sales channel, provided the Korean VAT-registered exporter clears the goods through Korea Customs Service, ships them outside Korea under a foreign transport contract, and obtains foreign currency proceeds from a non-resident buyer. For offshore digital services and intangible rights supplied to a non-resident customer (including game content, digital licences, and certain online services), zero-rating is possible when the supply is made to a foreign recipient under a foreign sales contract, payment is received in foreign currency, and the consumption or use occurs outside Korea; digital services consumed in Korea by Korean recipient require 10% VAT.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service export declaration (수출신고필증) filed through UNI-PASS
Commercial invoice issued from the Korean seller to the overseas buyer
Packing list describing the goods, quantities and export shipment details
Ocean Bill of Lading or Air Waybill, or a courier proof-of-despatch scan for international small parcel DTC shipments

Foreign exchange bank export settlement certificate (export proceeds purchase/sale certificate) or equivalent inward remittance record showing receipt of the foreign currency amount by the Korean entity
Order records, Shopify transfer order and payment gateway transaction history demonstrating the offshore buyer, payment card or alternative payment rail, and absence of Korean delivery address
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS and Korea Customs Service will disallow the 0% rate if the export paperwork is incomplete, contradictory, or not retained for the statutory period, and will reclassify the supply as domestic taxable at 10% VAT with interest from the original filing date. False or unsupported zero-rating exposes the exporter to additional tax penalties under the Value-Added Tax Act, including an extra tax of up to 40% of the under-reported taxable sales in cases of fraudulent overclaim, and to criminal liability under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act (조세범처벌법) punishable by imprisonment or fines up to three times the tax evaded. The clawback period is generally five years from the original tax return, extended to ten years in fraudulent or undisclosed cases, and the responsible tax representative may also be held secondarily liable.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (The Central Bank of the Republic of Korea), administered in cooperation with the Ministry of Economy and Finance as the foreign-exchange policy authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a liberalized but regulated convertibility system. The Korean won is freely convertible for genuine current-account transactions such as export proceeds, service fees, ecommerce settlements, and ordinary operating disbursements; however, capital-account flows -- nonresident equity injections, external loans, overseas investments, and financial derivatives -- are subject to ex-ante notification, post-reporting, or approval supervision under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Nonresidents and Korean entities are expected to comply with real-demand documentation at authorized foreign exchange banks. There is no blanket surrender requirement for export receipts, but incoming foreign exchange must be cleared through an onshore foreign exchange bank, and the corporate treasury may retain foreign currency only in a registered foreign-currency deposit account. Profit remittances are generally permissible once audited accounts and tax clearance are evidenced, but the bank will require the shareholder resolution, dividend payment proof, withholding tax certificates, and a foreign-exchange declaration to verify the capital and profit transaction. Domestic fintech/EMI wallets are not substitutes for licensed foreign-exchange banks for corporate treasury, because the FX notification and real-name financial transaction framework requires a regulated nexus.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be settled within one year from the date of exportation unless the authorized foreign exchange bank approves an extension for delays caused by default, dispute, or exchange controls in the buyer's country. There is no fixed statutory percentage requiring mandatory conversion to KRW; exporters may maintain foreign currency balances in onshore foreign-currency deposit accounts, but any conversion or utilization requires an underlying contract and foreign-exchange bank reporting if above the reporting threshold.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMI platforms that are not licensed under Korea's Electronic Financial Transactions Act and are not authorized foreign-exchange banks have low corporate treasury viability for a Korean-resident Yuhan Hoesa. They may be used indirectly as settlement processors for ecommerce sales, but they cannot legally open the primary KRW corporate operating account, cannot clear inbound FDI capital, and cannot provide the foreign-exchange declaration needed by customs and the central bank. Any offshore EMI payout must ultimately be routed through a domestic licensed bank or payment gateway, otherwise the entity will face FX violation risk and blocked remittances.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Statutory directors and authorized signatories should plan to appear physically at a Korean commercial bank branch for the initial corporate account opening and compliance interview. Remote consular proxy opening is not a standard Korean banking practice; although some banks allow a locally resident officer under a notarized and apostilled power of attorney, the statutory director's identification, ownership structure, and business explanation are usually mandatory and best satisfied by physical presence. Non-resident directors may complete supplemental video verification, but the bank compliance officer still requires original corporate registration documents, company seal certificate, and real-name verification under the Real Name Financial Transaction Act.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO holds controlling ownership in the Korean LLC with limited economic footprint in Korea and no local directors/financial records.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled certificate of incorporation and constitutional documents; Korean corporate registry abstract naming the Yuhan Hoesa's registered address and representative; full UBO KYC pack (passport, proof of residential address, tax identification, birth certificate, source-of-wealth statement with tax returns); notarized board resolutions; foreign investment notification receipt issued by KOTRA or the authorized bank; prior bank reference letters and audited financial statements showing legitimate capital origins.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency low-ticket DTC sales settled by Shopify Payments, PayPal, and Stripe generate aggregated remittances that cannot be matched to individual customer contracts or typical export invoices.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Merchant/PSP agreements with Shopify, PayPal, and Stripe; 12-month settlement statement or payout ledger; order-level transaction export showing SKUs, sale dates, amounts, customer countries, and shipping addresses; refund/chargeback and dispute logs; export declarations or customs receipts for cross-border parcels; integration/backend screenshots showing the link between the webstore and the payment rails; a written business narrative explaining digital DTC operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large sum deposits from foreign payment processors and ecommerce platforms trigger 'third-party payment' red flags because the remitter is not the actual buyer and may fall outside the bank's internal transaction limit.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PSP buy-flow and payout routing documentation; merchant settlement reconciliation schedule; platform payout reports; a signed compliance undertaking that aggregate processor settlements correspond to real underlying customer transactions; website storefront details; CRM and order database access for sampling; logistics tracking and delivery confirmation; any PayPal/Stripe compliance letters or virtual account statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Activity spike due to seasonal global DTC sales creates an inconsistent cash-flow pattern inconsistent with a small LLC, leading to enhanced EDD or SAR referral.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed treasury forecast linking marketing/paid-ad campaigns to weekly sales peaks; customer acquisition cost reports; Shopify Analytics or Google Analytics export; inventory procurement and supplier invoices; warehouse logistics records; export/import manifests; income tax filings; shareholder and director identity reiteration; and a factual transaction-volume explanation that matches website traffic, order counts, and entity scale.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity capital for the Yuhan Hoesa should be structured as foreign direct investment under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, with the non-resident shareholder filing a prior notification at KOTRA or through an authorized foreign exchange bank. The capital remittance is transmitted by SWIFT MT103 to the company's dedicated foreign currency escrow/current account at a Korean Tier-1 bank, with remittance information identifying the investor, the Korean company, the acquisition of shares/equity, and the FDI foreign-exchange purpose code. After receipt, the bank issues the foreign exchange declaration confirmation, the entity completes the paid-in capital increase registration with the court registrar, and an external accountant verifies the capital in the statutory capital verification certificate.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational disbursements for suppliers, digital advertising, and logistics should be cleared via SWIFT MT103 from the Korean bank account to the beneficiary's bank, supported by the underlying invoice and a foreign-exchange payment declaration. For formal B2B purchases and high-value consignments, documentary trade instruments remain permissible: commercial letters of credit issued by the bank (SWIFT MT700/MT710) under ICC UCP600 rules, and documentary collections (D/P and D/A) using shipping documents through correspondent banks. Ecommerce refunds and chargebacks are channeled through the PSP settlement system. All outbound transactions above reporting thresholds must be reported to the Ministry of Economy and Finance as required and evidenced by contracts, tax invoices, customs declarations, or purchase orders.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore KRW/USD deliverable forward contracts with an authorized domestic foreign-exchange bank covering genuine current-account exposure, including forecast DTC export revenue and payable flows

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts undertaken by the corporate treasury only with bank approval and documentary proof of underlying export/import exposure; speculative offshore NDF positions are not permitted for the Korean entity
FX swaps for hedging short-term foreign currency liquidity mismatches on export collections and supplier payments

Currency swaps limited to foreign-currency debt and FDI-related capital flows with the same bank, subject to board approval, credit assessment, and MOEF/Bank of Korea reporting where the exposure exceeds regulated thresholds

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and local income tax surtax return, including financial statements and supporting tax schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via HomeTax electronic filing; local income tax surtax to the competent municipal or provincial local government
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 31 of the year following the calendar fiscal year end; statutory deadline is within 3 months after fiscal year end, with a one-month extension available for qualifying taxpayers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under-reporting penalty of 20 percent of the unpaid tax, or 40 percent in cases of intentional concealment; daily late-payment interest of 0.022 percent; forced collection and seizure of corporate assets; revocation of tax clearance certificates; criminal referral under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act in serious cases

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quarterly value-added tax prepayment and final returns, including the electronic tax invoice ledger
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via HomeTax electronic filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar quarter filings: Q1 due April 25, Q2 due July 25, Q3 due October 25, Q4 due January 25 of the following year; small businesses below the statutory turnover threshold may file on a semi-annual cycle due January 25 and July 25
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharge of 10 percent of unpaid VAT; daily late-payment interest of 0.022 percent; penalty of 2 percent of supply value for missing or incorrect electronic tax invoices; repeated default can lead to seizure of bank accounts and NTS cancellation of the business registration

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Convening and holding the annual general meeting of members and approval of the annual financial statements, including balance sheet, income statement and appropriation of profits or losses
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate governance obligation under the Korean Commercial Act; approved statements must be retained at the registered office and, for externally audited companies, filed with the Financial Supervisory Service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the close of each fiscal year, no later than June 30 for calendar-year entities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct monetary penalty for a private company, but dividend distributions made without approved statements are voidable; directors and managers remain personally liable to the company and its members; audit-obligated companies are separately subject to financial supervisory administrative penalties

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory external audit report and audited financial statements for companies exceeding the mandatory audit threshold
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) via DART electronic disclosure system; audited financial statements also appended to the corporate income tax return filed with the NTS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 14 days after the annual general meeting or, if no general meeting is held, within 14 days after approval by members; in all cases no later than the corporate income tax return due date for calendar-year entities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of up to KRW 50 million, approximately USD 38,000, for failure to file or late filing under Article 24 of the Act on External Audit; non-compliance also impairs tax loss carryforwards and increases the risk of tax assessment adjustment by NTS

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual payroll income-tax withholding reconciliation and employee end-of-year tax settlement report, applicable if the company employs personnel
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via HomeTax electronic filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 10 of the year following the calendar tax year for the annual aggregate withholding return; monthly salary withholding deposits are due by the 10th day of each following month
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 0.5 percent of the unwithheld amount per day; failure to withhold renders the corporate representative personally liable; an additional tax of 5 percent of unwithheld tax may be assessed

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Amendments to the commercial registration for changes in registered office, manager or representative, or membership quotas; no annual renewal registration is required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Commercial Registration Office of the Korean court under the Supreme Court administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 14 days after the occurrence of a registrable change; transfer of membership quotas must also be contemporaneously recorded in the statutory register of members
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late registration exposes relevant officers to administrative fines and renders the unattested change ineffective against bona fide third parties; unregistered changes also impede tax refunds and VAT credit claims

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Article 4 of the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and its Presidential Enforcement Decree, an independent external audit by a licensed Korean CPA or audit firm is mandatory if, at fiscal year-end, the company (i) is listed on a Korean securities market; (ii) has total assets of KRW 12 billion, approximately USD 9 million, or more; (iii) has total assets of KRW 7 billion or more and satisfies a prescribed employee count, liability or turnover criterion under the Enforcement Decree; or (iv) falls within an additional statutory category such as a financial holding company or a company with certain registered securities. A Yuhan Hoesa operated as a Shopify DTC brand is exempt until the relevant asset, turnover or employment thresholds are exceeded.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Applicable accounting standards: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) for listed companies and, by election, for large non-listed companies; Korean GAAP, in the form of Korean Accounting Standards aligned with IFRS for SMEs, for non-public small and medium-sized entities. All standards are issued by the Korean Accounting Standards Board and require accrual-basis financial statements including a balance sheet, income statement, statement of changes in equity, cash flow statement and notes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not require a separate annual UBO declaration for a private Yuhan Hoesa. The obligatory ownership record is the statutory register of members, which must contemporaneously record full legal names, identification or passport data, number of quotas held and acquisition or transfer dates. Any transfer or pledge of a membership quota is effective against the company only upon entry in that register. Registrable changes, including a change of manager, transfer of control through quotas, or relocation of the registered office, must be filed with the commercial registration court within 14 days. The 30-day reporting window is not a Korean statutory deadline for membership transfers; the binding deadlines are the 14-day court-registration period and, for non-resident transferors, the 15-day capital gains tax return window under the Income Tax Act. Annual confirmation of ownership is effectively achieved through the annual general meeting review of the register and, where required, by the external auditor's confirmation in the audit file.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members listing the full identity and quota history of each member
Register of Directors and Managers including appointment, resignation and domicile details
Register of Charges, Pledges, Mortgages and Encumbrances over membership quotas
Minute Book of General Meetings of Members and Manager Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 to 2,000 per annum, reflecting the market range for a virtual Korean office or corporate liaison and agent service; no statutory government fee is assessed for maintaining a registered office, but a physical Korean address is required
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 to 20,000 per annum for a typical unlisted Korean SME operating an online DTC business; the precise certified audit fee depends on transaction volume, total assets, employee headcount and any consolidation requirements

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 21% top statutory corporate income tax rate (taxable income exceeding KRW 20 billion); plus 10% local income tax surcharge, aggregate top rate 23.1%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SME preferential rates (9% up to KRW 200 million; 19% from KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion); R&D tax credit up to 25-30%; investment tax credits for facility investment; special incentives for Free Economic Zones; no patent box regime but IP-derived income may qualify for certain expensing benefits; DTC export income eligible for general business tax credits; consideration of sign-off on foreign tax credits

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Korean Corporate Income Tax Return (Form No. 2 of the Corporate Tax Act) submitted electronically through the National Tax Service HomeTax portal (hometax.go.kr)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year (e.g., March 31 for a calendar-year end); for a non-resident corporation with no domestic place of business, the filing deadline is the same, but additional schedules are required

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification number, legal entity name, business address, Korean Standard Industrial Classification code (KSIC 4791 - Internet Retail), fiscal year-end, and number of shareholders
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations must provide the treaty residence country, domestic withholding agent details (if any), and attach a certificate of incorporation, articles of association, and registration of domestic place of business (if applicable). Ensure that the effective management place (Box 1-E) is consistent with actual decision-making substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2: Statement of Comprehensive Income (Sales & Cost of Sales)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report gross sales from Shopify DTC stores, including payments via Shopify Payments, PayPal, and Stripe; deduct cost of goods sold, shipping, platform commissions, credit card fees, and sales returns
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Korean domestic entity, all worldwide income is declared. If the entity is classified as a non-resident with a permanent establishment, only Korean-source income is reportable. Revenues denominated in foreign currency must be converted using the official base rate on the transaction date; adjust for accrued revenue and unreconciled settlement batches from payment gateways.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add back non-deductible expenses (entertainment beyond statutory limits, fines, penalties, provision for bad debts not recognized); deduct tax-exempt income (e.g., intercorporate dividends received) and tax-free deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border intercompany management fees, brand royalty payments, and marketing recharge from related parties must be substantiated with arm's length transfer pricing documentation and economic substance evidence. Lack of supporting documentation will lead to add-back of the expense and a 30% penalty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4: Loss Carryforward & Tax Base Computation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute taxable income after applying net operating loss carryforwards (NOLs), small and medium enterprise loss carryback provisions, and other deductions from gross income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: NOLs are carried forward 10 years under the Corporate Tax Act. Losses incurred in a Korean permanent establishment can only be offset against Korean-source taxable income. For startups in the DTC space, carryforward order and priority (oldest first) must be strictly observed; failure to attach a NOL statement (Form 5-2) will result in disallowance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate tentative corporate income tax using the progressive rate schedule; add local income tax surcharge (10% of corporate tax); deduct prepaid taxes, foreign tax credits, and tax credit incentives; aggregate to final net tax payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify eligibility for foreign tax credit relief under the Korea-<treaty> DTA and complete Form 45, 'Foreign Tax Credit Application'. If the shareholder is in a treaty jurisdiction and has a permanent establishment in Korea, the dividend distribution may be subject to a branch profits tax regime; apply the applicable treaty provision.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Details of all payments made to non-residents during the fiscal year: dividends, interest, royalties, technical service fees, rent, and other income; withheld amounts and tax rates applied
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach Schedule 12 (Declaration of Non-Resident with Domestic Business Place) and Schedule 13 (Withholding Tax Recap). For dividend remittances to a non-resident parent, compute withholding on the entire gross dividend before any shareholder-level deductions; claim reduced treaty rate by attaching Tax Residency Certificate and Form 23-2 'Application for Exemption/Reduction of Withholding Tax' at the time of payment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 20% of unpaid corporate income tax if filed within one month after deadline; 30% if filed after one month. Surcharge for under-reporting: 10% of the unreported amount if unintentional, 40% if intentional. Omission of a required schedule: 10% penalty on the related underpayment. Interest on unpaid tax: 1.2% per month, capped at 36% per annum. Criminal false filing/submission: imprisonment up to 5 years and fine up to KRW 50 million.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% (20% national dividend withholding tax + 2% local income tax surcharge) on gross dividends paid by a Korean corporation to a non-resident corporate shareholder, unless reduced under an applicable Double Taxation Agreement (DTA)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, the non-resident recipient must: (1) obtain an original Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the tax authority of the residence country, not older than 6 months; (2) complete Form 23-2 'Application for Exemption or Reduction of Withholding Tax' before the payment date; (3) provide a statement that there is no permanent establishment in Korea to which the dividends are effectively connected; (4) disclose the ultimate beneficial owner (prove no nominee or back-to-back arrangement). The Korean payer must submit the documents to the local tax office within 30 days of the withholding. If the application is incomplete, the statutory 22% rate must be withheld. Subsequent refund may be made via a tax ruling petition.

stage_6.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: statutory 22% (20% + 2% local); treaty rates typically 5-15% (e.g., 10% for financial institutions, 15% for any other interest). Royalties: statutory 22% (20% + 2% local); treaty rates typically 10-15% for industrial, commercial or scientific royalties, and 15% for copyright royalties; source taxation of royalties may be excluded under the 'income from immovable property' analogy if the IP is registered in Korea. Documentation includes TRC, beneficial ownership statement, and a license agreement aligned with the transfer pricing rules.
